summaries.demographer: Milton Wells is a 73-year-old white, non-Hispanic, U.S.-born man living alone in a paid-off home in northwest Oklahoma City (Q51, Q58, Q86-Q89). He is divorced, has two adult children and three grandchildren, and is not cohabiting with a romantic partner (Q05, Q84). His highest education is a high school diploma, and he is retired from handyman and maintenance repair work (Q65, Q90). His household income is modest but stable, based mainly on Social Security, savings, and occasional retirement withdrawals (Q61, Q74, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Milton shows strong loss aversion and planning discipline, especially around debt avoidance, emergency savings, and refusing to put a desired Grand Canyon trip on a credit card (Q62, Q63, Q82). His choices are habit-driven: he budgets monthly, checks balances weekly, combines errands, cooks at home, and tracks volunteer funds with spreadsheets, though receipts are a recurring weak point (Q17, Q56, Q81). He values independence and future security more than consumption, delaying camera gear and other discretionary purchases when costs rise (Q60, Q64). Peer influence operates mainly through trusted family, church, and senior-center networks rather than mass media (Q25, Q42, Q48).
summaries.political_scientist: Milton is a regular voter and a moderately strong Republican who describes himself as conservative but practical (Q23, Q95, Q96). He supports fiscal responsibility, personal accountability, public safety, and traditional values, while also endorsing community obligations toward seniors, disaster victims, and families in need (Q24). His institutional trust is selective: he respects police and doctors but wants accountability, local facts, and less cable-news conflict (Q25-Q27, Q42). His civic identity is local and service-oriented, expressed through church repair work, senior-center mentoring, and careful participation in elections (Q16, Q23, Q47).
summaries.psychologist: Milton presents as conscientious, methodical, practical, and identity-anchored in usefulness, reliability, and hands-on competence (Q01, Q65, Q109). He copes with stress through routine, prayer, outdoor activity, repair tasks, model building, and social contact rather than substance use (Q38, Q43, Q45). He experiences loneliness and low moods, especially in winter evenings or when health limits activity, but maintains emotional stability through church, family, friends, and volunteer obligations (Q43-Q45). His self-concept is shaped by aging with limits while preserving independence, service, and dignity (Q34, Q83, Q108).
